Lighthouses are tall structures, typically at the entrance to a harbor or along a coast, equipped with a bright light to serve as a navigational aid for maritime pilots at sea or in inland waterways.
The height of a lighthouse is often determined by the curvature of the earth and the desired range of the light, with taller structures allowing the beam to be seen from greater distances.
Modern lighthouses are largely automated and may be replaced by GPS and other electronic navigation systems, though many remain as historic landmarks and tourist attractions.
